cs.t: I really like rtings.com. I am using the Dell S2721QS for my home office. It is a cheaper version of the S2722QC and does not have the integrated USB hub. Before WFH, at the office, I used the U2723QE which is excellent. But for coding work it is visually indistinguishable from the S2721QS (and probably the S2722QC). The S2721QS has a slight issue with "ghosting" or "fading" near the edges. However it is only an issue if looking at the monitor from a far angle which is rarely the case for me at my desk. I'm not sure if this has been fixed in the S2722QC. Dell monitors consistently impress me with their top-notch construction, sturdiness, and dependability. One of my pet peeves with monitors and TV's in general is panel gap which is the space from the end of the panel to the plastic frame. Dell monitors usually minimize that. Just to share my setup: 2x 4k monitors, portrait and landscape, both at 125% zoom (effectively 3072x1728). IDE is primarily opened on the landscape. Portrait monitor is split into 3 sections: browser, Outlook/Teams/Slack and terminals. I use Stardock Groupy [1] to combine Outlook/Teams/Slack into "one window" and Windows PowerToys FancyZones [2] to manage the split. [1]  https://www.stardock.com/products/groupy/  [2]  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/powertoys/fancyzon...  From my vantage point, it's a precarious time to consider a new monitor or TV.
